summary: T15-05 passes. I ran all five checks exactly as written and each exited 0 (web test 432 passed, `vitest run server/api` 270 passed). The four routes answer only with problem+json. The status rule is 404 when manifest.json does not hold the record or file, and 501 when it lists a file that has no schema. `family=model` is gated by `modelFamilyAccess`, which refuses unless G5 is PASS and carries the Predicted label when it allows. `/compare` imports no @terraluna/core. The paths changed are inside the story's files list. The same range also touches ralph batch, log and script files, which I took as orchestration bookkeeping and did not review. The mock-bundle body scan, the OpenAPI problem responses and the "no @terraluna/core" test were judged from reading the code, the story notes and the test run, not from reading each test body.

checks.criterion: Routes matches, windows, compare and model exist with validated parameters, and respond with problem+json saying the record or file is not in bundle <bundle_version>. The 404/501 rule is documented in a code comment and tested.
checks.evidence: The 404/501 rule is the header comment at unavailable.ts:1-15. app.ts registers all four routes. matches.ts:56-92 validates body (enum earth), family (enum terrain|radar|model), limit (1 to 500, default 50) and cursor, with `.strict()`. unavailable.test.ts (22 tests) and matches.test.ts (68 tests) pass.

checks.criterion: family=model returns an explanatory problem+json. It never returns distances with the mock bundle. Model-family data must carry the Predicted label and be refused while G5 is not PASS, and a test pins the refusal.
checks.evidence: model.ts:36-61 `modelFamilyAccess` refuses when the manifest names no model, or when manifest.model.g5 or the single validation.json G5 record is not PASS. It returns the Predicted label only when allowed. matches.ts:124-128 calls it for family=model. unavailable.test.ts uses G5_PASS and G5-not-PASS bundles. model.test.ts (16 tests) passes. The mutation checks in the progress notes were not re-run by me.

checks.criterion: /compare is not computed in this batch. No @terraluna/core call is made and no Derived-on-request value is produced. The story notes record that on-request computation waits for T10.
checks.evidence: compare.ts imports no @terraluna/core, and the handler only throws notInBundle or notServedYet (compare.ts:58-75). The prd.json notes item (3) and the progress.txt entry record that on-request computation waits for T10 and real fingerprints. That the test checks the absence of @terraluna/core was taken from the notes; I did not read that test body.

checks.criterion: A test scans the response bodies of these routes against the mock bundle and asserts no numeric distance, rank or fingerprint field appears.
checks.evidence: unavailable.test.ts:81 defines RESULT_KEY (/distance|rank|fingerprint|embedding|score|percentile|similar|match/i). The test at line 103, 'carry no numeric distance, rank or fingerprint field, for any valid request', passes in the run.

checks.criterion: The routes appear in the OpenAPI document with their problem+json responses.
checks.evidence: Each route uses `unavailableResponses` (unavailable.ts:57-77), which declares 400, 404, 500 and 501 with the application/problem+json schema. The routes are registered through api.openapi in app.ts. The tests in the passing suite that check the OpenAPI document were not read.
`next typegen`, `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc --noEmit -p server/api` completed with exit 0.
ruff and mypy passed. The turbo lint and typecheck tasks were 4 successful, all cache hits.

pytest 404 passed. The turbo web (432) and schema (157) tests were cache hits, replayed from the shared cache rather than re-executed. The web 432 count matches my direct run of `pnpm --filter @terraluna/web test`.

findings.claim: The story's own commits also changed prd.json, progress.txt and the ralph scripts (new-batch.sh, prompt.md, ralph.sh, review.sh). Those are outside the story's files list.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat across the range shows scripts/ralph/* and logs/agents/*.jsonl alongside the apps/web/server/api files. The prd.json change is the review-state bookkeeping, and the ralph scripts are orchestration. I did not inspect the script changes.

resolution.reason: The paths outside the story's files in aba5ce1..71f9f7f were not changed by the author. scripts/ralph/batches/t15-api/prd.json and progress.txt are this batch's story list and progress log, which the author prompt (section 2) allows, and the prd.json change is the review.state bookkeeping. scripts/ralph/new-batch.sh, prompt.md, ralph.sh and review.sh came in only through c51a7a6 (Merge branch 'ralph/tooling' into ralph/t15-api, an orchestrator merge). git log --first-parent over the range for those files lists only that merge, and its second-parent commits (a6dfe83, c02fb70, c97ca63, 3dc1c63) are ralph tooling work. The only commit in the range touching logs/agents/2026-11-14/t15-api/*.jsonl is 7300356 (chore(ralph): record t15-api loop state after branch restore), the loop's own state commit. No product file outside apps/web/server/api changed.

findings.claim: /windows/{id} and /compare answer 501 for any valid id once a window or comparison file is listed, so an unknown id and a known id look the same. The 404-for-unknown-ids criterion is met only for the case where the bundle lists no such file.
findings.evidence: The windows.ts header comment and the prd.json notes item (2) state this, and it follows from no WindowRecord schema existing. I did not read the windows tests to see whether they pin it.

resolution.reason: This is the same defect as codex-r1-1, fixed in 88300c2 (tests in 0151847). 404 now covers every id the manifest can rule out, not only bundles that list no window or comparison file. Examples: an id outside manifest.targets when only targets.json is listed, and a comparison whose comparisons/<a>.json and comparisons/<b>.json are both unlisted and whose two windows no listed file could hold. 501 remains only when a listed file could hold the record. In practice that is a windows/<body>.json top-N file, whose ids cannot be read without parsing a file that has no schema. windows.test.ts and compare.test.ts pin both sides.
